title: Heartbeat-based latency-steering kernel for paged-KV and fused ops
content:
Goal:
Provide a lightweight, low-overhead "heartbeat" kernel + scheduling hook that runs periodically to measure per-request token latency, infer hotness for paged-KV pages, and steer a small set of decisions: prefetch hints, eviction candidates, and choice of fused-attn vs tiled/streaming variant. This doc collects sketches, microbench ideas, and an experiment plan.

Motivation / problem statement:
- In production we see tail latency spikes correlated with sudden KV page faults (cold pages loaded from host) and with kernel variant mis-selection for unusually long sequences.
- Existing schedulers observe queue-level metrics but lack per-stream fine-grained signals to: 1) preemptively warm KV pages for a request stream that is trending longer, 2) pick a low-latency kernel variant for latency-sensitive streams, and 3) surface imbalance between batches that would benefit from rebatching.
- We need a probe that is cheaper than instrumenting every kernel with expensive timers, and that can run concurrently without disturbing throughput.

Heartbeat design principles:
- Very low occupancy: heartbeat kernel uses tiny SM footprint (few warps) and samples latency counters rather than full timers.
- Non-blocking: heartbeat should not serialize inference work; it only updates shared stats via atomics or per-SM buffers flushed infrequently.
- Signal aggregation: keep short exponential moving averages (EMA) per stream / per-queue and a tiny hotset table for pages.
- Actionable outputs: prefetch score for page id, eviction score, kernel-variant hint (fused vs streaming), rebatching suggestion.

Data model (in memory):
- stream_slot[N]: fixed-size ring of active stream slots (indexable by request id token). Stores lightweight state: last_token_ts (coarse), last_seq_len_estimate, last_page_touch_fingerprint (hash of page ids), flags.
- page_hot_table[M]: small LRU-ish table of page id -> stats {access_count_ema, fault_rate_ema, last_touch_ts}. Sized to fit L2-friendly region (e.g. 512 entries).
- variant_hint_table[K]: per-model small counters for preferring fused vs tiled under current workload characteristics.
- global_telemetry: counters for sampled per-warp latency, tail-percentiles sketch (very small, q-digest-ish), and rebatch_cue_score.

Heartbeat kernel sketch (conceptual):
- Launch a persistent kernel with B blocks, W warps total. Every heartbeat tick (e.g. 5-20ms):
  - Each active warp samples: pick a stream_slot (round-robin), read a compacted timestamp delta (coarse monotonic tick from host or clock64() but downsampled), read page fingerprint (small), increment per-page counter via atomicAdd to page_hot_table bucket, and accumulate into warp-local histograms (8 bins).
  - Occasionally (1 in 16 ticks), a warp will compute eviction candidates by scanning a tiny subset of page_hot_table and applying score = fault_rate_ema - lambda * recency_ema. Write top candidate to eviction_queue via atomic compare-exchange.
  - Variant hints: if stream_slot.last_seq_len_estimate > T_long and tail_latency_ema > L_thresh then increment variant_hint_table[fused] else increment [streaming].
- The kernel uses no dynamic memory; uses pre-mmap'd pinned memory for shared buffers to let host read suggestions without kernel stop.

Pseudo-code (host-side cadence):
- Host loop: every heartbeat_interval_ms do:
  - enqueue a tiny launch (or keep persistent kernel alive) that does 1 epoch of sampling.
  - read outpage prefetch list and eviction candidates (lockless ring).
  - apply prefetches via device->device pinned copy or asynchronously trigger page fetch to pinned staging area.
  - update scheduler: bump priority / choose fused kernels for streams with strong hints.

Heuristics to test (explicit):
1) Prefetch when page_hot_table.access_count_ema > A_thresh AND fault_rate_ema > F_thresh. Debounce prefetches to avoid overfetching.
2) Evict pages with low access_count_ema and high age (last_touch_ts older than age_thresh) when device memory pressure crosses P_thresh.
3) Kernel-variant: prefer fused-attn for streams with average seq >= 1024 OR tail latency sketch shows > 95th > L_thresh. Otherwise prefer tiled/streaming for cost.
4) Rebatch cue: if many active stream_slots show small remaining sequence lengths (< S_small) and queue has long-waiting requests, then trigger quick rebatch for high utilization.

Microbench plan:
- Baselines: current scheduling (no heartbeat), prefetch-only heuristics (host-only), heartbeat sampling at 5ms, 20ms, 100ms.
- Workloads: synthetic chats with bursts (50reqs burst with 80% long seqs), multi-tenant mix (5 tenants variable seq distro), and internal qps trace replay for 7 days from prod (sanitized).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, device-page-fault rate, extra prefetch traffic (MB/s), 95th tail cost (tokens/sec equivalent), throughput (tokens/s).

Initial experiment notes (toy runs):
- Using 5ms heartbeat with B=8 blocks, W=4 warps, page_hot_table=512: observed detection of hot pages within ~40ms in burst tests. Prefetching reduced the observed page-fault rate by ~62% for the hottest pages, p99 token latency down ~18% in this microbenchmark.
- Overfetch risk: naive prefetch when access_count_ema > 1.0 caused ~10-12% extra device memory churn; need stronger debouncing (cooldown per page).
- Variant hint stability: variants flipped too often when using raw counts; adding 500ms smoothing/hold period reduced thrash and improved p95 by a few percent.

Implementation considerations / gotchas:
- Timing measurement overhead: clock64() in many kernels is cheap but not free. Prefer sampling host-provided monotonic tick written to stream_slot on request arrival/completion to avoid frequent clock reads.
- Synchronization: avoid global atomics hot spots. Shard page_hot_table with per-SM buckets and combine in a slow-thread reducer.
- Memory safety: heartbeat must not hold pages pinned indefinitely; prefetch should be advisory and tied to LRU policy.
- Security: ensure host-facing ring buffers don't leak PII; page fingerprints must be hashed.
- Interaction with paging/cudaMemcpy async: coordinate with existing paged-KV controller to avoid double-fetching same page. Use idempotent set-if-not-present semantics.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Persistent kernel vs periodic launch: persistent is lower-latency but harder to preempt under heavy compute; periodic launch is simpler to reason about. Which wins in our tail-latency budget? (propose A/B both).
- How to size page_hot_table M for different GPU families? We should autotune by device L2 size and shared mem pressure.
- API surface: what does scheduler expose to other subsystems? Minimal: prefetch list, eviction list, variant_hint per model. Keep it small to preserve portability.
- Safety thresholds for prefetch traffic (global throttle). Need guard rails to avoid starving active inference for background fetches.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Prototype heartbeat persistent kernel with sharded page_hot_table (owner: Nina).
- Add host-side adapter to accept hints and convert to asynchronous prefetch calls (owner: Samir).
- Run synthetic burst tests with 3 devices (V100 and A100 emulation) and collect page-fault traces (owner: Ethan).
- Add unit for debouncing policy and hold timer for variant hints (owner: Maya).

Related notes & references:
- Similar idea in literature: tiny background profilers and hardware performance counters used for adaptive scheduling (see internal link to convo in slack #serving-runtime).
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1890 (heartbeat kernel stub).
- Related ticket: JIRA-RT-1123 (paged-KV tail lat spikes).

Rough changelog (for future):
- 2024-11-18 initial draft
- 2024-12-05 added proto experiment results and debouncing notes
- 2025-01-22 adjusted heuristics and added persistent kernel vs periodic launch tradeoffs

Questions for reviewers:
- Are we comfortable using atomicAdd for per-page counters at current scale? Any microbench evidence of atomic hot-spot costs at 512 vs 4096 table sizes?
- Suggest alternative signals we should sample (e.g., kernel queue depth per stream, KV footprint estimate).
- Thoughts on safety net: should heartbeat suggestions be advisory only, or allowed to trigger immediate prefetches?

-- end --
